narrative.title: Fingerprinting Packet Runs with XOR Signatures
narrative.scenario: A deep packet inspector folds the bytes of each packet into a single integer fingerprint and keeps the packets in arrival order. A security rule triggers on any contiguous run of packets whose combined XOR fingerprint equals a known signature. Count how many such runs exist in the capture.
narrative.inputFormat: An integer N, an array A of N non-negative fingerprints, and an integer B, the signature to match.
narrative.outputFormat: The number of contiguous subarrays of A whose bitwise XOR equals B.

testCases.explanation: The whole capture folds to 2, and so do the two single-packet runs holding 2, giving three matches.
Four distinct runs fold to the signature, including overlapping runs that share packets.

hintLevels: Level 1: XOR of a run equals the fold of one prefix combined with the fold of the other, and the operation that undoes a fold is the fold itself.
Level 2: Keep the running fold and a frequency table of folds already seen; each packet contributes the number of earlier folds equal to fold XOR signature.
Level 3: Seed the table with fold 0 so runs beginning at the first packet are counted, and remember a signature of 0 makes every all-zero run a match, including overlapping ones.
